include: Public synchronous PF SQL API with SQLite backend
Project-owned worker attempts, current physical executions, indexed heads and bounded history
Existing CLI/MCP and service-independent file-only composition
Explicit deterministic worker snapshot migration and recoverable projection
defer: Migration/refactoring of accounting, events, hooks, Ledger, chat and canonical Work YAML
Server drivers, ORM, SQL builder, dynamic driver registry, async/pools, RAG, scheduler, global updater
authority: Run/assignment stages remain YAML-owned; task_id is the existing assignment id, not a new entity
Capsules/prepared inputs and substantive artifacts remain immutable files
Project SQL owns interpreted execution facts after cutover; status.json is generated
Receipts are evidence, not independent lifecycle writers; Ledger session ownership is unchanged
This is transitional topology, not completed consolidation

topology.project_profile_path_base: actual flow root; default path is data/pf.sqlite3, never .pf/data relative to flow root
topology.workplace_future: data/pf.sqlite3 relative to explicitly selected workplace; not activated by this slice
topology.legacy: Events/hooks/accounting retain current files, IDs and application_id; do not redirect legacy factories to PF main
topology.identity: Migration and fresh SQL initialization require explicit nonempty manifest project.id. Reject root-name fallback as unstable; never silently mint/change existing IDs.

semantics: Construct/import/factory is cold: no connect, mkdir, bootstrap or singleton. Closed mapping sqlite -> SQLiteDriver; only required capabilities listed above are mandatory for execution repository.
SQL dialect is SQLite with ? bound values. No portability claim for SQL text; future backend replaces repository adapter, not domain ports.

Database.read uses ro/noncreation, BEGIN snapshot, rollback/close on exit. transaction uses existing rw only, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, commit on success, rollback on BaseException; no implicit create, nested transaction or retry.

Only SchemaManager uses create/admin DDL/PRAGMA. initialize rejects existing/nonempty/foreign stores; apply can add an absent known namespace to a valid envelope but cannot upgrade an existing namespace in R02. Same version/checksum is no-op; drift/future version refuses.
WAL is set/verified during initialize/apply; FULL and FK=ON are verified for writes. No weakening durability. No connection/cursor escapes; ro is enforced, not inferred from SQL verb.
Driver admin channel is private to SchemaManager. Public SqlSession is for parameterized repository DML/queries, not an arbitrary untrusted SQL sandbox; no home-grown SQL parser/security promise.
stream batch_size 1..1000; execute_many <=10000 rows and statement.params must be empty; close cursor on early exit; sessions are operation/thread-bound.

deadline is absolute time.monotonic; SQLite busy timeout is min(profile timeout, remaining budget), progress handler checks query deadline. A 100 ms DB default does not enlarge the 500 ms guard deadline.
No DB transaction across Popen/wait, signals, output reads, backup, full scan or projection I/O.
DatabaseError(code: str, retryable: bool = False) contains no raw exception/SQL/params/private target. Existing public adapters retain their payloads and exit/error mapping.

Database.read/transaction and factory normal use require concrete store_id. Only SchemaManager.inspect may use DatabaseTarget.identity.store_id=None to discover an existing main envelope while still checking scope/owner/application_id; discovery does not bind a project or authorize data reads. Missing returns missing, never creates.

profiles.shape: optional database: {profiles: {<id>: {scope, driver, path, timeout_ms}}, defaults: {project_main?: <id>, workplace_main?: <id>}}
profiles.type: DatabaseProfile(scope: Literal['project','workplace'], driver: Literal['sqlite'], path: str, timeout_ms: int = 100); DatabaseConfig(profiles: immutable mapping[str,DatabaseProfile], defaults: immutable mapping[str,str])
profiles.validation: Unknown keys/options rejected; profile IDs [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}; relative contained paths only, no CWD/env expansion, '..', symlink/reparse escape; timeout_ms exact int 0..30000. First slice has no application scope, driver_options, codecs or registry.
profiles.inheritance: Project config permits only project profiles and project_main. Reject name collisions and workplace overrides. Absent database stays absent in to_dict/get/update/reset and old payloads; preserve old parsing and unknown-key errors.
profiles.binding: Profile grants no access. Factory requires resolved host-authorized target and matching profile scope/path. Construct only; SchemaManager checks physical identity. Binding pins store_id/path; config reload must not switch existing execution target. Changed path/identity requires explicit maintenance.
profiles.defaults: Without section use nonpersisted project profile data/pf.sqlite3; do not initialize workplace storage. Do not serialize profiles just to use defaults.

envelope.namespace_rules: Physical envelope version only; domain schemas use pf_schema_versions. Namespace constants execution@1 (W3), execution_migration@1 (W4). No accounting/events/hooks namespaces registered in R02.

envelope.rule: Verify application_id/user_version/store_id/scope/owner before domain access. Namespace DDL+checksum registration is atomic. All statements/checksums are code-owned; no arbitrary namespace/SQL from user config.

table_columns.execution_heads: project_id TEXT; run_id TEXT; task_id TEXT; latest_attempt INTEGER NOT NULL; next_attempt INTEGER NOT NULL; projection_dirty INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK IN (0,1); PK(project_id,run_id,task_id); latest key FK execution_attempts
table_columns.execution_current: project_id TEXT; run_id TEXT; task_id TEXT; attempt INTEGER; PK(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt); FK execution_attempts; UNIQUE(project_id,run_id,task_id)
table_columns.execution_receipt_admissions: project_id TEXT; run_id TEXT; task_id TEXT; attempt INTEGER; launch_token TEXT; kind TEXT; sequence INTEGER NOT NULL; checksum TEXT NOT NULL; PK(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt,launch_token,kind); FK execution_attempts

constraints: All key columns NOT NULL; attempts/revisions>=1, generations>=0, next_attempt>latest_attempt, next_history_seq>=1. JSON is validated canonical text by adapters, not by new SQLite JSON extension requirement.
phase/outcome/collection CHECK enums fixed by DTO; outcome is NULL or completed/failed/timed_out/cancelled/unknown_exit/lost/blocked. Status payload schema_version remains 1.
execution_state singleton belongs to this project; physical envelope owner and all row project_id must match. Scoped repo never queries another project.

execution_current contains exactly starting/running/stopping/unresolved, no prepared/absent. Enforce in repository transaction plus invariant tests; absence outcome update and current deletion commit together.
Index execution_history(project_id,history_seq) WHERE history_seq IS NOT NULL; unique nonnull launch_token; index execution_projection_dirty(project_id,run_id,task_id) WHERE projection_dirty=1.

Heads allocate next attempt inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE; allocation does not enumerate attempt directories. Refuse next allocation while current ownership exists. A prepared/manual attempt without launch has no current row.

First proven physical absence allocates monotonic history_seq once; later collection/receipt updates never reorder history. high_water is captured from next_history_seq-1 in first page snapshot; limits 1..1000.

All writes compare generation and expected revision, increment record revision and execution_state revision. Identical admitted receipt is a no-op even after revision advanced; same sequence/different hash is conflict, lower sequence is stale no-op.

Admission table stores only latest accepted sequence/hash per kind per launch, not every periodic heartbeat. Process identity immutable after attachment; exit payload cannot turn different PID birth into same process.
ack_projection changes only projected_revision and heads dirty when latest key/revision still match; it does not increment lifecycle revision. Older attempt cannot overwrite latest projection.
execution.current_query: SELECT selected non-history columns FROM execution_current c JOIN execution_attempts a USING(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt) WHERE c.project_id=? ORDER BY c.run_id,c.task_id,c.attempt LIMIT ?; fetch limit+1; indexed point reads only of current attempts
execution.current_semantics: Read state and rows in one snapshot. More than limit, unknown coverage, unsupported/missing DB or deadline -> incomplete/unknown, never truncation presented as exact zero. Guard does not reconcile, scan history, read completed receipts or send signals.
lifecycle: allocate -> prepared; reserve_start CAS -> starting + current, commit before any Popen
Popen succeeded -> exact process receipt attachment -> running; failure proven before child creation -> absent/failed + history
Controller death before attachment retains starting/unresolved and current; no TTL auto-reclaim
request_stop sets stopping; signal success alone never removes current. Observe wrapper and owned descendants; unresolved observation remains active.
Terminal exit code and full tree absence -> absent + outcome + atomic current removal. If absence proven but no trustworthy exit -> absent/unknown_exit; do not invent exit success.
Collection retains existing receipt/capsule/output/semantic-refusal checks; collection failure does not revive a process. Completed/uncollected is physically inactive.
Late exact-old-attempt evidence may update that old record only; never use load_latest as mutation target.

receipts.transport: Retain compatible heartbeat.json/exit.json top-level fields; add private launch identity to producer evidence only, not public status payload. New SQL-managed launches require capable existing wrappers; legacy route accepts old receipts as before.
receipts.fields: schema_version=1 plus project_id/run_id/task_id/attempt/launch_token, receipt_kind, sequence, observed_at, process identity where applicable; canonical content checksum excludes its checksum field
receipts.publication: Write attempt-specific process/heartbeat/exit receipts atomically at existing captured attempt paths, not shared-latest filenames for identity. Controller may retain legacy latest projections. Wrapper publishes its process identity before launching target; target/tree ownership is observed separately.
receipts.security: Token is random uuid4 hex per physical launch, not a permission. Receipt paths, prepared input and scope checks remain enforced. Imported receipts missing launch identity cannot authorize a new SQL launch.
receipts.os: W3 owns Windows process creation time and Linux boot_id+/proc start ticks adapters. Unsupported/denied/changed process or unprovable descendants -> unknown. No new psutil dependency or PID-only success. Prove tree absence with existing handle/owned process group/verified tree; if unavailable retain unresolved.

projection.rule: payload_json is the validated compatibility DTO in the same canonical transaction, not a second editable owner; preserve imported unknown fields as provenance and projection extensions where already present. No launch_token/generation/revision added to public status.
projection.mapping: prepared retains planned/ready/manual_required/blocked; starting -> starting; running -> running; stopping -> cancelled with existing stop-request failure_reason while SQL current remains; unresolved -> running with uncertainty reason (or retained cancelled after stop); absent uses outcome. Collected retains completed; failed collection projects failed; semantic refusal retains existing completed/refusal flow, never marks accepted.
projection.publication: Under existing task lifecycle lock read authoritative latest DTO, atomic replace status.json, then ack CAS. Failure leaves heads.projection_dirty=1; retry only indexed dirty heads or exact task, no full history rebuild. CLI/MCP/continuation consume SQL after cutover even if projection stale.
projection.timestamp: last_heartbeat_at derives from accepted timestamp/fresh evidence, never mere file existence or observation wall-clock.

ddl: CREATE TABLE execution_state(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1),project_id TEXT NOT NULL,generation INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(generation>=0),authority TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(authority IN ('legacy','sql')),readiness TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(readiness IN ('importing','ready')),active_coverage TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(active_coverage IN ('complete','unknown')),revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(revision>=0),next_history_seq INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(next_history_seq>=1),migration_id TEXT,plan_checksum TEXT)

CREATE TABLE execution_attempts(project_id TEXT NOT NULL,run_id TEXT NOT NULL,task_id TEXT NOT NULL,attempt INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt>=1),launch_token TEXT UNIQUE,revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(revision>=1),generation INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(generation>=0),phase TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(phase IN ('prepared','starting','running','stopping','unresolved','absent')),outcome TEXT CHECK(outcome IN ('completed','failed','timed_out','cancelled','unknown_exit','lost','blocked')),collection TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(collection IN ('pending','collected','failed','refused')),process_json TEXT,history_seq INTEGER UNIQUE CHECK(history_seq>=1),payload_json TEXT NOT NULL,projected_revision INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(projected_revision>=0 AND projected_revision<=revision),source_path TEXT,source_checksum TEXT,semantic_checksum TEXT,PRIMARY KEY(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt))

CREATE TABLE execution_heads(project_id TEXT NOT NULL,run_id TEXT NOT NULL,task_id TEXT NOT NULL,latest_attempt INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(latest_attempt>=1),next_attempt INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(next_attempt>latest_attempt),projection_dirty INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(projection_dirty IN (0,1)),PRIMARY KEY(project_id,run_id,task_id),FOREIGN KEY(project_id,run_id,task_id,latest_attempt) REFERENCES execution_attempts(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt))

CREATE TABLE execution_current(project_id TEXT NOT NULL,run_id TEXT NOT NULL,task_id TEXT NOT NULL,attempt INTEGER NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt),UNIQUE(project_id,run_id,task_id),FOREIGN KEY(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt) REFERENCES execution_attempts(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt))

CREATE TABLE execution_receipt_admissions(project_id TEXT NOT NULL,run_id TEXT NOT NULL,task_id TEXT NOT NULL,attempt INTEGER NOT NULL,launch_token TEXT NOT NULL,kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('process','heartbeat','exit','absence','spawn_failed')),sequence INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(sequence>=0),checksum TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt,launch_token,kind),FOREIGN KEY(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt) REFERENCES execution_attempts(project_id,run_id,task_id,attempt))
CREATE INDEX execution_history ON execution_attempts(project_id,history_seq) WHERE history_seq IS NOT NULL
CREATE INDEX execution_projection_dirty ON execution_heads(project_id,run_id,task_id) WHERE projection_dirty=1
execution.schema_authority: ddl is normative; table_columns is explanatory. EXECUTION_SCHEMA is a SchemaDefinition(namespace='execution',version=1,statements=tuple(ddl),checksum=canonical schema digest). W3 owns it; W4 consumes exact exported constant.

admission.reuse: Inject existing registry_file_lock; preserve its permanent OS guard and dead-owner-only reclamation. Do not import tools/processforge.py into Core. No coordinator service or additional database.
admission.order: workplace admission (when enrolled) -> project admission -> existing task lifecycle lock -> SQL transaction. If singleton lifecycle guard needed, acquire after workplace admission and before project. Never hold runtime.state_lock/host.state_lock while acquiring an interprocess gate; short memory locks only inside already-acquired gate.
admission.start: Every CLI/MCP/Inspector/scheduler/supervisor spawn path acquires admission; verify binding/readiness/generation and Runtime instance state, commit reservation before releasing admission. Popen occurs after committed reservation, outside SQL transaction; task lock serializes attach/reconcile.
admission.shutdown: Set in-process shutdown_check briefly, release memory lock, acquire workplace admission within existing 500 ms budget, verify instance and registered routing, acquire project admissions sorted by stable project_id then routing path. Read complete current snapshots; legacy projects retain old bounded file observer. Under admission publish stopping durably before gate release. A reservation is visible before guard, or start sees stopping and refuses.
admission.registration: Enroll/unregister/route/cache changes use same workplace admission then project gate; import any already-current standalone executions into routing coverage before publishing enrollment. An enrolled project cannot claim standalone to bypass an unavailable workplace gate. Unregister refuses unresolved physical ownership.
admission.stopping_recovery: Use existing Runtime instance/service state as stopping fence, no new persistent coordinator. Starts are refused while matching owner is alive/stopping. Clear/recover only after exact instance death/normal completion under same admission and existing singleton protocol; elapsed TTL alone is not proof. No daemon is needed for file-only CLI when no active owner exists.
admission.unknown: Any gate timeout, unreadable routing, missing identity, unknown old writer, unknown current/tree state, incomplete migration or stale registration makes guard running=null and preserves runtime_busy_or_activity_unknown. Existing owner_changed is retained. No silent fallback after SQL binding.
admission.limitation: Old binaries do not acquire new admission. Online mixed-version writer safety cannot be guaranteed: explicit maintenance exclusion of those binaries is a prerequisite, otherwise cutover is blocked.

routing.fields: {schema_version:1,project_id,store_id,profile_id,target_relative_path}; project-relative/flow-relative target only, immutable after successful binding unless explicit maintenance
routing.owner: W4 writes migration binding; W3 writes fresh binding through explicit new-project initialization and reads it in composition. SQL transaction alone decides readiness/authority; binding routes and pins expected identity only.
routing.legacy_selection: No binding and no execution namespace at resolved default/configured main target -> legacy, with existing behavior. If target exists, inspect without DDL. Corrupt/foreign/unknown target or execution namespace without binding -> blocked, not legacy.
routing.sql_selection: Binding exists -> require exact matching DB/envelope/namespace/project/store_id and ready SQL authority; missing/partial target blocks. Never recover from status.json when binding exists. Before SQL cutover a pending binding intentionally blocks ordinary execution until resume/explicit abort.
routing.fresh: Only successful explicit init_project apply creating a new flow root may initialize empty store, binding and ready SQL generation=1 with complete active coverage. Use initialization transaction/repair path; existing root including --force is never classified fresh from empty history. Reads/status/doctor/config/imports create nothing.
routing.failure: Fresh DB/binding publication is recoverable, not filesystem+SQL atomic: publish binding first, then initialize; crash leaves blocked pending binding until explicit repair. Pre-cutover abort validates no SQL authority/new commits before removing only owned binding.
routing.profile_change: Binding pins target/store. Config reload mismatch fails without reconnecting a new empty target. Project move preserves project.id/store_id and relative target; reject identity collisions and active/unknown old ownership.
routing.missing_identity: If manifest lacks explicit project.id, migration returns project_identity_required; operator must persist the existing intended identity through normal project configuration before planning, not accept a new root-derived ID.

migration.shared_import: W3 import_legacy runs only in caller-owned W2 write session and execution_state importing/legacy. It does not commit, connect, publish or enable authority. Each source_fact is (project-relative path, byte checksum, semantic checksum), aligned with records. W4 writes checkpoint in the SAME session; batch <=256. Normal domain ports never accept SqlSession.
ddl: CREATE TABLE execution_migrations(migration_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,descriptor_checksum TEXT NOT NULL,plan_checksum TEXT NOT NULL,store_id TEXT NOT NULL,source_generation INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(source_generation>=0),target_generation INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(target_generation>source_generation),state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(state IN ('planned','backed_up','importing','verified','ready')),checkpoint INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(checkpoint>=0),manifest_checksum TEXT NOT NULL,evidence_relative_path TEXT NOT NULL,backup_manifest_checksum TEXT,last_error_code TEXT)
migration.descriptor: migration_id; descriptor_version=1; source_format=worker-status-json; source_schema_versions=[1]; target_namespace=execution; from_schema_version=0; to_schema_version=1; min_reader_capability=execution-storage-v1; min_writer_capability=execution-storage-v1; transform_files[{relative_path,sha256}]; transform_checksum. Pin final transform bytes at implementation, never fabricate a release version/hash.
migration.checksums: Canonical JSON everywhere: UTF-8, sorted object keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, no trailing newline in digest input. SHA256 prefixed sha256:. Descriptor checksum hashes full descriptor; transform checksum hashes canonical ordered transform_files. Plan checksum hashes descriptor_checksum + explicit project_id + ordered relative source path/size/hash manifest + store_id + target schema checksum + source/target generation + skip policy. Exclude operation UUID/time/evidence absolute paths.
migration.scanner: Only explicit inspect/plan/apply/resume inventories legacy status.json, attempt DIRECTORY NAMES and direct bounded process/heartbeat/exit evidence needed for quiescence. Do not read stdout/stderr, report or prepared-input bodies to reconstruct missing history. Preserve source JSON unknown fields/original bytes. Reject duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, NUL, unknown schema and identity mismatch.
migration.attempt_policy: Absent/invalid attempt is blocked, not guessed as 1. Import observable latest snapshots only, no invented overwritten attempts. Heads floor = max(imported attempt, valid existing numeric attempt directory names)+1; names are allocation evidence, not reconstructed history. Ambiguous names/identity conflicts block.
migration.sort: Source relative paths ordered by raw UTF-8 byte order, no locale/casefold/NFC normalization. Stable sequence is import order, not asserted chronology. External spool/manifest, batches <=256, no all-history envelopes/IDs in RAM.
protocol: inspect/plan read only, except explicit evidence_dir may retain declared scan evidence; no destination DDL or binding writes. Return blocked when old writers/quiescence cannot be proved. Apply revalidates all facts even if plan said safe.

Operator stops/disables all old writer entrypoints and confirms offline maintenance. This is a prerequisite, not a remotely enforceable flag. Acquire admission, publish project pending binding/freeze, release long-held admission for scan/backup/import. New capable writers see pending and refuse; old binaries must remain excluded.

Require zero proven current physical executions, no unresolved pre-spawn publication gap, stable source inventory and no legacy writer. A terminal status string or process PID probe alone is insufficient. Unknown legacy activity blocks; operator must establish quiescence, not use --skip-invalid.

Frozen exact sources+SHA256 manifest are retained exclusively under maintenance evidence; after restart recheck live sources against frozen manifest. Existing target: BackupPort.create+verify before first target DB mutation. Absent target is recorded. Backup bytes are WAL-aware via existing SQLiteBackupService; no new backup engine.

Initialize new main envelope or add missing execution namespaces to existing valid envelope explicitly using SchemaManager. Register execution_state importing/legacy generation=0 (or expected prior generation); do not enable new writers.

For each <=256 batch, import_legacy and checkpoint in same transaction. Same key+semantic/source hash -> no-op; different payload same key -> execution_identity_conflict and stop. Checkpoint never advances on failed batch.

Verify schema/checksum, integrity, FK, receipt/hash parity, import counts and replay=no-op; full manifest hash and live inventory unchanged; no unresolved current ownership. Historical completeness may be partial but active_coverage must be complete.

Reacquire workplace/project admission, verify pinned instance/routing/generation and source stability; CAS execution_state to authority=sql, readiness=ready, generation=target_generation, active_coverage=complete, plan_checksum; set execution_migrations ready in same SQL transaction. This commit is the only cutover point.
Publication of report/projections after commit may fail; readiness from SQL remains true. resume recognizes committed marker and repairs only owned derived output, never reimports JSON as new truth.
migration.readiness: History gaps do not mean current activity. First cutover requires quiescent current set=empty and complete coverage. No active-process takeover in R02; 400k fixtures with active executions test post-cutover operation, not live migration.
migration.backup_resume: Before reusing backup verify its manifest/hash, pinned store identity and relation to this plan/checkpoint. Do not overwrite/create a second arbitrary backup on resume. Drift refuses; successful import commits are recovered from checkpoint, not rolled back implicitly.
migration.quarantine: Exact frozen bytes/provenance/hash retained; conflicts always block. skip_terminal_invalid is only explicit, positively proved historical records; invalid state preventing exclusion of active work blocks even with flag.
migration.rollback: Before SQL cutover: explicit abort under admission with disabled new writers, verified no ready authority/new SQL commits, unchanged sources; preserve shared DB, remove only owned pending binding/namespace state if safe. After cutover: roll forward/resume; restore backup to NEW target via BackupPort and controlled binding switch with all writers stopped. No old-Core rollback after new SQL commits without separately qualified reverse export.
